headline: Risk-off tone builds as NQ futures slide 1.4%, VIX pops above 20 and the 10-year holds 5.13%

open.headline: Tech-led pullback expected at the open with defensives and value cushioning index losses
open.body: S&P futures at 7532 point to a soft open roughly 30 handles below Friday's 7561 cash close, with 7500 the first line of defense and 7450 the deeper support shelf. Megacap semis and AI-infrastructure names look heaviest after the 1.4% NQ futures drop, while the Dow's modest Friday gain suggests continued rotation into healthcare, staples and industrials. Expect a jumpy, headline-sensitive tape with VIX near 21 and thin conviction ahead of Tuesday's retail sales print.

newsCards.title: Yields Pin Valuations Near 5.13%
newsCards.body: The 10-year sitting just above 5.1% keeps the discount-rate math punishing for long-duration growth equities. Until the curve stabilizes, every rally in high-multiple tech is likely to be sold into.

newsCards.title: VIX Reclaims 20 Handle
newsCards.body: A 6.8% jump in the VIX to 20.62 signals dealers are paying up for downside protection into a data-heavy stretch. Sustained prints above 20 historically coincide with wider intraday ranges and faster factor rotations.

newsCards.title: Silver's 3.9% Air Pocket
newsCards.body: Silver down nearly 4% while gold slips only 0.4% points to a leveraged-long unwind rather than a change in the inflation narrative. Precious-metal miners and industrial-metal proxies should see outsized volatility at the open.

newsCards.title: Retail Sales on Deck Tuesday
newsCards.body: The advance retail and food-services report lands Tuesday at 8:30am ET and is the week's first real read on the consumer. A hot print would push yields higher and compound pressure on rate-sensitive growth names.

newsCards.title: FOMC Minutes Wednesday
newsCards.body: Wednesday's 2:00pm ET release of minutes from the Oct 27-28 meeting will be parsed for how divided the committee is on further easing. Any hawkish dissent language could reprice the front end and cap equity bounces.

newsCards.title: AI Capex Trade Loses Momentum
newsCards.body: NQ futures underperforming S&P futures by roughly 75 basis points reflects concentrated de-risking in the AI complex. Power, cooling and data-center derivatives tend to carry the highest beta when this trade unwinds.

newsCards.title: Crude Slips Below $88
newsCards.body: WTI easing 1.2% to $87.53 removes a modest inflation tailwind but also trims energy-sector earnings momentum. The move is consistent with a broader growth-scare tone rather than a supply development.

newsCards.title: PCE and Payrolls Frame the Month
newsCards.body: The next genuine catalysts are the PCE price index on Wed, Nov 25 and the Employment Situation on Fri, Dec 4. Positioning is likely to stay defensive and range-bound between now and that Thanksgiving-week inflation print.

opportunity.reason: With the Dow outperforming and VIX rising, managed care offers low-beta earnings visibility that is largely insulated from the AI-multiple unwind. It is a classic vehicle for rotation-driven defensive flows in sessions like this.

avoid.reason: High-beta AI data-center names are the most exposed to both the 5.13% 10-year and a 1.4% drop in NQ futures. Chasing a dip here risks catching the sharpest leg of a leveraged-positioning unwind.
